details: U.S. President Donald Trump landed in Beijing for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on May 13, 2026. While trade and AI are on the agenda, the ongoing war with Iran and China's "four red lines" in relations are expected to overshadow discussions. The war's estimated cost is $29 billion, contributing to rising inflation and gas prices in the US.
title: Trump Arrives in China for Summit, Iran War Overshadows Talks

details: The United States has rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal, leading to escalating tensions in the Middle East. President Trump described the ceasefire as "on life support" and called Iran's counter-proposal "garbage." Reports indicate a significant escalation in the Strait of Hormuz, with US Navy destroyers reportedly attacked by Iranian missiles and drones, pushing oil prices above $100 per barrel and fueling US inflation, with gas prices up over 28%.
title: US Rejects Iran Ceasefire, Strait of Hormuz Tensions Escalate

details: US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.6% month-over-month in April, matching expectations but pushing the annual inflation rate to 3.8%, the highest in over 2.5 years. This surge is primarily driven by elevated oil prices. In response, traders have largely priced out any Federal Reserve interest rate cuts for 2026.
title: US CPI Jumps to 3.8% Annually, Rate Cuts Unlikely in 2026

details: Financial services giant Charles Schwab has launched spot Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) trading for select retail clients as of May 13, 2026. This move signifies increasing institutional adoption and integration of cryptocurrencies into mainstream financial platforms.
title: Charles Schwab Enables Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum Trading

details: At the FII Priority Miami forum on March 12, 2026, former U.S. President Donald Trump described Bitcoin as "powerful" and endorsed crypto payments, advocating for "innovation-friendly" stablecoin regulation. This marks a significant shift from his previous skepticism towards cryptocurrencies and signals potential supportive policy directions.
sourceName: CryptoRank (and BBC for background on Trump's shift)
title: Trump Calls Bitcoin "Powerful," Backs Crypto Payments
